newsitem.title: USA: Hotel hopes to boost business trade.
newsitem.headline: Hotel hopes to boost business trade.

text.p: Work officially begins this week on the first major hotel to be built in Miami Beach for three decades, a project developers and city officials hope will boost the business trade in one of the United States' most fashionable areas.
The $135 million, 800-room hotel is being built by Loews Hotels, with the opening planned for the summer of 1988.

The project involves renovating the St. Moritz Hotel to its former Art Deco splendor and building 700 new rooms in a 17-story tower. The architects promise to blend classic Florida architecture with the new Miami beach spirit.

The Loews Miami Beach Hotel is located in the heart of the Art Deco district, once a rundown area which in recent years has undergone a rennaissance into a district of trendy restaurants, nightclubs and shops.

But the lack of business-standard accommodations was harming the Miami Convention Centre, prompting the Miami Beach City Commission to seek partners for a new luxury hotel. Loews beat five other bidders to secure the project.
"Loews hotels is very opportunistic but also conservative when it comes to expansion," said Chief Executive Officer Jonathan Tisch, who was in Miami for Thursday's ground-breaking ceremony.
"But given the uniqueness of the site, the growth of Miami Beach and the city's involvement it was something we couldn't pass up," he said.

The city will provide $29 million, Loews $40 million and $66 million more will come in a loan from a consortium of banks headed by Bankers Trust, Tisch said. The Miami Beach Redevelopment Agency is providing $50 million in incentives.
Tisch said he expected 70 percent of the trade to be from group business and 30 percent from individual travelers, and hopes hotel will turn a profit as soon as possible.
"The early response from groups has been terrific." Tisch said, noting that there are 700,000 tentative room bookings to date.
Tisch himself is no stranger to Miami or its hotels. His father built the Americana, now the Sheraton Bal Harbour, 40 years ago.
"I have fond memories of that place. I learned to swim in the pool at the Americana in the early 1960s. I met President Kennedy there in 1962."

Loews Hotels is part of Loews Corp., which is controlled by the Tisch family. Its interests include CNA Insurance, Lorillard tobacco company, Bulova Corp. and 14 hotels and resorts in the United States, Canada and Monaco.

Loews is also developing two other projects in Universal City, Fla., in partnership with MCA Inc. They are the 750-room Portofino Hotel, slated to open in 1999, and the 1,200 room Royal Bali Hotel, set to open in 2000, Tisch said.
